text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A UK meta-regression of 236 elasticities from 16 studies finds no overall practically significant adverse employment effect from minimum wage increases.","cited_pids":["5f591435f1d8#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"The same UK meta-regression flags residential home care as a possible exception with a genuine negative employment effect.","cited_pids":["5f591435f1d8#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"A review co-authored by Arindrajit Dube reports that most US minimum wage studies find no job losses or only small disemployment effects.","cited_pids":["f3df8a818b8c#0"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"A study of low-wage jobs finds the overall count of such jobs essentially unchanged over five years after minimum wage increases.","cited_pids":["e0f83db9d354#1"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"A Congressional Budget Office estimate of a $15 federal minimum wage projected about 1.4 million fewer jobs.","cited_pids":["6de9116294ca#3"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"A study of federal minimum wage increases found significant negative effects on employment and income growth for targeted low-skilled workers.","cited_pids":["ab2ba547baf0#1"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"A review of the literature notes that disemployment effects from minimum wage increases are stronger for the least-skilled groups.","cited_pids":["39a319a8bc00#2"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"An analysis of teen unemployment links minimum wage hikes to higher teen joblessness.","cited_pids":["59c7d48f7cbf#0"]}]}
